token_revoked.title: HAIM can no longer reach your installer
token_revoked.description:
Your installer has revoked the key this instance used to report in. Nothing is being sent any more, and no alerts about this instance will reach them.

This is usually deliberate - a change of installer, or a key that had to be replaced. If it is not, ask them for a new pairing code and set the integration up again.

site_inactive.title: HAIM monitoring is paused
site_inactive.description:
Your installer's HAIM account has archived this instance, or their subscription has lapsed. Nothing is being sent while that is true.

The component will check again every six hours on its own. If you were expecting to be monitored, this is worth a phone call.

clock_skewed.title: This system's clock is wrong
clock_skewed.description:
The date and time on this machine are impossible - earlier than this component was made, or more than a day away from the real time. It usually means the machine cannot reach a time server, which a Raspberry Pi without a battery-backed clock needs at every start.

Until it is fixed, HAIM uses the time of your installer's server for the events it sends. Other things on this system rely on the clock too - certificates, backups, automations that run at a given hour - so it is worth fixing: check the network and the time settings of the host.

abort.issue_ignored: Understood. You can read this again in the HAIM documentation at any time.

confirm.title: What HAIM sends out of this house
confirm.description:
This system is monitored by the installer who looks after it. So that you know exactly what that means, here is what leaves this house and what does not.

**What is sent**

How many entities, devices, automations and dashboards exist. How many entities are currently unavailable. Which version of Home Assistant is installed and which updates are waiting. Whether the last backup worked. How busy the processor, the memory and the disk are. The names of the *types* of integration in use - `zha`, `mqtt` - and the names of installed add-ons.

Error log messages are sent at the level chosen when this was set up, which is currently **{log_level}**. Before any message leaves, it passes through a filter that removes access tokens, email addresses, IP addresses, network names and web addresses containing passwords.

**What is never sent**

The names of your devices. The names of your rooms. What any device is doing, now or in the past. Your energy consumption. Camera images. Anything about the people who live here.

Nobody can see your system remotely unless you approve it, each time, and only for as long as you allow.

The code that does all this is public and can be read by anyone: github.com/usehaim/haim-agent
